floor_history.headline: Recon: floor 9 re-confirmed (verdict C, 91/90 insns); gap mapped to 2 axes (1 combine-fold BF68[0] + 8-op sched1 reorder); fresh finding: D_8009BF68 externs disagree (array vs fn-ptr).

Structural session: killed H-A1/H-A2 (combine offset-0 fold) and H-B1 (sched1 tie-break) with ~17 measured variants; floor holds at 9. Both axes are now mechanism-pinned, remaining levers are non-stru

frontier.hypothesis: H-A3 (cross-function): target materializes &D_8009BF68 because the ORIGINAL translation unit referenced the address of D_8009BF68 a second time (giving the address pseudo >1 use so combine keeps it in a register). This is not reachable by any single-function decl/access shape (all fold). The lever, if it exists, is a source-structure fact coupled to sibling func_8007D3F8 (only other user, queue ~43) or a different TU/function boundary.
frontier.mechanism: combine.c will not propagate a multi-use address pseudo into a (mem reg); a genuine second use of &D_8009BF68 forces the materialized la;lw form target has.
frontier.next_probe: When func_8007D3F8 matches, read its committed D_8009BF68 decl and check whether that shape (plus any shared access) makes the address multi-use. Otherwise, look for a second &D_8009BF68 reference the original had (e.g. an address compare / store) that pure-C would emit; verify with sandbox.

frontier.hypothesis: Axis B (8 ops) is a genuine sched1 critical-path tie that structural levers cannot flip; the closing lever is likely non-structural (directed permuter over the arg-setup region, or an RA-steering form that changes the dead read's allocation without a pin).
frontier.mechanism: fmt (chain length 1) must outrank the deadread->BF7C->subu->call chain in sched1 priority; no pure-C statement reordering changes those chain lengths without altering volatile semantics.
frontier.next_probe: Hand off to a non-structural modality: directed permuter (PERM_* over the first debug_printf arg block, fresh-seed) or a register-allocation-focused pass; measure whether any form schedules fmt ahead of the dead read (target byte order at 6E4EC-6E520).
